title: Blush Framework plugin manifest
description: A local plugin's plugin.json: its name, label, namespace, service provider, and the classes autoloaded for it.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema editors check this file with.

name.description: The plugin's name, the key it's known by: vendor/name, such as "acme/gallery". Its folder is extensions/{vendor}/{name}, so it must match the folder. Without it, the name in the composer.json beside this file is used; for a Composer package, it's the package name.

label.description: The plugin's title, as people read it. Without one, it's shown by its name.

namespace.description: The namespace the plugin's components, icons, and translations go by, such as "gallery" for gallery/slideshow. No two installed extensions may share one. Without one, it's the name with hyphens for the "/" and any ".", such as "acme-gallery".

provider.description: The class name of the plugin's service provider. Leave it out for a plugin without one, such as one that only loads autoload.files.

autoload.description: What to autoload, as composer.json says it. Without it, the autoload in the composer.json beside this file is used.

psr-4.description: Namespace prefixes, each ending in a backslash, and the folders inside the plugin their classes are in, such as {"Acme\\Gallery\\": "src/"}.

files.description: Files inside the plugin loaded once when it runs, such as ["src/helpers.php"].

require.description: What the plugin needs, as composer.json says it, with version constraints: php, blush-dev/framework for Blush, ext-{name} for PHP extensions, and other plugins by vendor/name. A plugin whose requirements aren't met doesn't run. Without it, the require in the composer.json beside this file is used.

authors.description: Who made the plugin, as composer.json lists authors. Without it, the authors in the composer.json beside this file are used.

role.description: What they did, such as "Developer" or "Designer".

license.description: How the plugin may be used, as an SPDX identifier such as "MIT". Without it, the license in the composer.json beside this file is used.
